audit_scope.description: This batch covers EL logic (EVM runtime, EOF container validation, KECCAK256 opcode, EVM tracing, wallet chain addition) and CL logic (FOCIL inclusion lists, attestation aggregation, sync committee gossip, P2P discovery).

out_of_scope: EVM Trace Output Generation (EIP-7756, tooling only)

execution_layer.threat: Submit malformed transactions, deploy malicious EOF containers, trick wallet into adding malicious chains

consensus_layer.threat: Submit invalid inclusion lists, conflicting attestations, gossip mutation attacks on committee indices
Flood sync committee subnets, send malformed discovery packets, eclipse attacks via routing table poisoning

consensus_layer.entry_point: External APIs (RPC endpoints provided by dapps)
consensus_layer.threat: Provide incorrect chain ID data, TOCTOU attacks on chain validation

misclassified_entities.reason: The transaction mempool is an internal node component, not an external entity. It does not reside outside the system boundary.
EIP-7199 is a meta-governance EIP about linter rules with no runtime protocol impact. The EIP contributor is not an external entity interacting with the Ethereum protocol.
Trace consumers read output data from the system; they do not send data INTO the system. This is a data sink, not an external source of input requiring trust modeling.

trusted_external_entities.name: Inclusion List Submitter via P2P Gossip
trusted_external_entities.rationale: SignedInclusionList messages arrive via unauthenticated P2P gossip. Any peer can submit them. Committee membership, committee root, and BLS signature must all be validated before acceptance.

trusted_external_entities.name: Block Producer / Proposer via P2P
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Block proposers submit blocks that must satisfy inclusion list compliance. Proposers are validators but their blocks are received via unauthenticated P2P and must be fully validated including IL compliance checks.

trusted_external_entities.name: Contract Deployer via Transaction
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: CREATE/CREATE2 transaction (eth_sendRawTransaction RPC or P2P mempool)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Any user can deploy contracts. EOF containers and legacy bytecode must be fully validated at deployment time. Malicious bytecode is expected.

trusted_external_entities.name: Message Caller via Transaction/Internal Call
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Any external account or contract can initiate message calls. Call data, target address, and value are all untrusted inputs. Jump destination validation and opcode restrictions provide runtime safety.

trusted_external_entities.name: Peer Node via CL Gossipsub
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Peer nodes on the P2P gossip network are unauthenticated. All messages (sync committee messages, attestations, contributions) require full validation: slot checks, subnet membership, duplicate detection, BLS signature verification.

trusted_external_entities.name: Validator via Attestation Gossip
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Validators submit attestations via P2P gossip. Committee membership must be verified to prevent gossip mutation attacks (EIP-7549). Aggregated signatures require pairing-based verification.

trusted_external_entities.name: DApp via wallet_addEthereumChain RPC
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Dapps can request adding arbitrary chain configurations to user wallets. All parameters (chainId, rpcUrls, chainName) are untrusted. Chain ID format validation, HTTPS URL enforcement, RPC chain ID verification, and explicit user consent are all required.

trusted_external_entities.name: Remote Node via Discovery v5 UDP
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Discovery nodes respond to FINDNODE queries with ENR records. UDP is unauthenticated and unreliable. ENR records must be verified via their embedded signatures. Routing table poisoning and eclipse attacks are possible threat vectors.

trusted_external_entities.name: UDP Network Transport
trusted_external_entities.rationale: The underlying UDP transport is unauthenticated, unreliable, and potentially adversarial. Packets require header unmasking, protocol ID verification, and AES-GCM decryption/authentication before processing.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: Inclusion List Validation Pipeline (committee membership, committee root, BLS signature)
boundary_edges.security_assumption: All three validation checks must pass: (1) submitter is a member of the inclusion list committee for the specified slot, (2) inclusion_list_committee_root matches the Merkle root of the actual committee, (3) BLS signature is valid under DOMAIN_INCLUSION_LIST_COMMITTEE.

Block proposals must be validated for inclusion list compliance. Non-compliant blocks (missing forced transactions) must be deprioritized by fork choice. The union of all valid inclusion list transactions must be checked.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: EOF Container Validation (magic bytes, version, section order, type section, code sections, size limits, stray bytes)
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Full EOF container validation is required at deployment time: magic byte check, version validation, section order enforcement, type section size divisibility, code section minimum size, MAX_INITCODE_SIZE limit, and no stray bytes. Legacy bytecode must also undergo jump destination analysis.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: EVM Execution Context (message call handler, jump destination validation)
boundary_edges.security_assumption: All call data and target addresses are untrusted. Jump targets must be validated against pre-computed valid_jump_destinations set. EOF opcode restrictions must be enforced (reject list). DELEGATECALL from EOF to legacy must fail. Invalid opcodes must cause execution revert.

Full validation pipeline required: (1) slot matches current slot within MAXIMUM_GOSSIP_CLOCK_DISPARITY, (2) validator belongs to the sync committee subnet, (3) no duplicate message from this validator for this slot on this subnet, (4) BLS signature over beacon block root is valid.

Full contribution validation required: slot check, subcommittee_index bounds, aggregation_bits non-empty, aggregator selection proof validity, aggregator subcommittee membership, and both selection proof and aggregate BLS signatures verified.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: Message ID Derivation (Snappy decompression, SHA256 message ID computation)
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Messages must be correctly identified via domain-separated SHA256 hashing. Valid Snappy decompression uses MESSAGE_DOMAIN_VALID_SNAPPY; failed decompression uses MESSAGE_DOMAIN_INVALID_SNAPPY. This separation prevents message ID collisions between valid and invalid messages.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: Attestation Gossip Validation (committee membership pre-cache verification)
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Committee membership must be verified BEFORE caching to prevent gossip mutation attacks. The committee_bits field (unsigned, outside signed data) must be cross-checked against actual committee assignments. This prevents attackers from modifying the committee index during gossip propagation.

Full parameter validation required: (1) chainId is valid hex format, (2) rpcUrls non-empty with HTTPS scheme only, (3) no duplicate chain, (4) eth_chainId response from RPC matches submitted chainId, (5) nativeCurrency object valid if present, (6) explicit user consent with requester identification and RPC exposure warning. The submitted chainId (not RPC-reported) must be used for signing.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: Discovery v5 NODES Response Handler (routing table update)
boundary_edges.security_assumption: ENR records in NODES responses must be verified via their embedded signatures. Routing table updates must respect k-bucket limits (max 16 per bucket). Stale nodes must be evicted via liveness checks (PING). Response size limited to 16 result nodes per FINDNODE.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: Discovery v5 Packet Processing (header unmasking, protocol verification, AES-GCM decryption)
boundary_edges.security_assumption: All incoming UDP packets must be: (1) header-unmasked using local node ID, (2) protocol ID and version verified, (3) message decrypted and authenticated via AES-GCM. Failed decryption triggers WHOAREYOU challenge for session establishment. Packet size must not exceed 1280 bytes.

coverage_analysis.notes: 3 entities from source files were reclassified as misclassified (EXT-MEMPOOL as internal component, EXT-EIP-CONTRIBUTOR as governance-only, EXT-TRACE-CONSUMER as data sink not source). All 9 valid external entities have at least one boundary edge. EXT-P2P-PEER-CL-GOSSIP has 3 boundary edges covering sync committee messages, contributions, and message ID derivation.
